title: Empty requirement
context: A methods paragraph has already given every assumption used in the comparison. This closing sentence supplies no further condition, example or action.
text: A fair evaluation must consider data access, reported outputs and statistical precision.
reason: The sentence repeats an unused generic requirement.
preserve: Keep the comparison assumptions already used in the argument.

title: Necessary theorem condition
context: A displayed bound contains 1/q. The proof assumes a strictly positive lower bound q0.
text: The estimate holds for success probabilities q >= q0 > 0.
reason: The lower bound is necessary for the stated estimate.
preserve: Retain q0, positivity and the denominator step that uses them.

title: Finite evidence expanded to a theorem
context: The study reports initial gradient variance for simulated systems from 8 to 40 qubits. It supplies no asymptotic proof.
text: These runs reached 40 qubits and therefore prove the model remains trainable at every size.
reason: The universal trainability conclusion exceeds the finite initial-gradient evidence.
preserve: Keep the tested sizes, initial gradient variance and observed trend.

title: Component transfer scope
context: A proposition permits transfer of feature parameters because the feature module has fixed size. Its classifier has separate size-dependent parameters.
text: The fixed feature module allows its learned parameters to transfer to larger instances.
reason: The statement stays within the component covered by the proposition.
preserve: Retain the component boundary and the proposition assumptions.

title: Unused fact in a sequence
context: The section asks why a predictor scales. The revenue statement has no later use in this argument.
text: The predictor improves test error. Its supplier also reports increased revenue.
reason: The revenue statement has no job in the research argument.
preserve: Keep the measured prediction evidence. Remove only the unused fact.

title: Finite trend with explicit scope
context: The cited plot reports initial gradient variance for the stated finite set of system sizes.
text: Initial gradient variance stays similar across the sizes in this study.
reason: The text states its empirical range and statistic.
preserve: Keep that range and statistic. Add a concrete limitation only when the evidence requires one.

title: Approved repetition
context: The author accepted a conclusion that repeats two current research questions before answering each one.
text: The conclusion returns to both research questions and presents the corresponding results.
reason: The repetition serves an approved reading task.
preserve: Keep the approved question wording, current source version and acceptance scope.

title: Duplicate roadmap
context: Adjacent sections each give the same paper outline. Both serve navigation alone. The author requested compression.
text: The next paragraph repeats the full section sequence stated immediately above.
reason: The repeated paragraph supplies the same reading guide.
preserve: Retain one accurate guide at the place where the reader needs it.

title: Undefined acronym
context: This is the first occurrence at the intended reader's entry point. The method has no earlier accessible definition.
text: APS improves the reported prediction scores.
reason: The reader needs the method name and identity at first use.
preserve: Expand Adaptive Projection Sampling, identify its role and retain only the supported result.

title: Appendix detail
context: The main text explains the estimator result and links to the appendix. The appendix contains the full proof and required assumptions.
text: The appendix derives the estimator and states the conditions for each step.
reason: The detailed derivation serves the appendix's checking role.
preserve: Keep the assumptions and full derivation. Match detail to this section's purpose.

title: Vague mechanism
context: The next paragraph must explain how a sampler turns measured outcomes into a prediction. Its model record gives the actual mechanism.
text: Our design clarifies the prediction interface.
reason: The text leaves the operation and output unnamed.
preserve: State the model's actual sampling operation and prediction output.

title: Predictor identity conflict
context: The supplied code averages simulated amplitude vectors before applying a nonlinear output function. It supplies no device density-mixture experiment.
text: The device experiment evaluates a mixture of density operators.
reason: The predictor and evidence type conflict with the implementation.
preserve: Retain reported numerical values while their computation remains undisputed. Reconcile model identity before revising the account.

title: Copied theorem with missing input convention
context: The source proof establishes equivariance for an augmented input whose edge schedule is transported under relabelling.
text: The source theorem gives equivariance for every unaugmented graph input.
reason: The claim omits the transported schedule needed by the proof.
preserve: Keep the valid theorem, augmented input and transport convention.

title: Unauthorised result replacement
context: The author requested wording and layout edits. An editor proposes replacing the approved result plot with a fresh local run.
text: Replace the main result plot with the new simulation output.
reason: A result replacement exceeds the authorised task.
preserve: Keep the approved asset while the author reviews the new run, version and purpose.

title: Research reason lost in compression
context: The author approved a reason for using simulation: it permits controlled comparisons. The revision brief asks for connected prose.
text: The shortened opening removes the controlled-comparison reason.
reason: The cut removes an approved part of the research argument.
preserve: Restore that reason and remove a separate redundancy if needed.

title: Concrete metric limit
context: A reported comparison uses a score computed only from coefficient magnitudes.
text: Flipping coefficient signs leaves this magnitude-based score unchanged.
reason: The sentence gives the exact information limit of the score.
preserve: Retain the distinction between magnitude agreement and sign agreement.
